comparator.name: Communication and Information Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The documented 2026–2027 Media and Journalism allocation totals 180 EC, including 30 EC of approved open study. This is a qualified comparison of that published academic content, not a certified progression route for 2026 entrants. Discourse and Social Interaction requires Discourse Analysis, which is absent from the route allocation. The applicable prerequisite, any extra credit or replacement, and consequent thesis access remain unverified. Future 2027–2028 and 2028–2029 recruitment revisions are provisional and are not substituted into this comparison. Adopted 2026–2027 OER Article 9.1 and the exact annual course list require a pass in Discourse Analysis before Discourse and Social Interaction. The first course is in the English Language and Media route but is absent from the Dutch Media and Journalism allocation. The published Formuleren course overlaps in discourse methods, but its explicit use as an entry requirement is for Interactie in Organisaties. Article 3.7 allows an individual examination-board exemption, not a cohort rule. The provisional 2027–2028 recruitment list omits Discourse and Social Interaction and lists Digital Deception and Redactionele innovaties, without an adopted replacement, credits or cohort bridge. The shown allocation has 60 EC each year, including 30 EC open study and a 12 EC thesis and colloquium pair. OER 9.1 requires passing all first- and second-year courses for the thesis and colloquium. The Dutch diagnostic and any required remediation gate Academic Skills, and 42 EC plus the designated skills and language conditions apply to ordinary first-year study advice. Orientation and language requirements add no credits. Open study has approval and level rules. Workshops and practicals normally require 80% attendance.

alternatives.concept: Study how moving images, language and stories shape public understanding. VU provides a dedicated newsroom, journalistic writing, conversation-analysis and thesis sequence beyond this broader media-studies response.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three independently supported directions: closest media/narrative inquiry; public trust and institutional communication; data/AI understanding of digital media. Their 37.5,30,37.5 EC pairwise differences arise from coherent methods and subjects. Stop at three; no additional career-only or platform-example programme is generated.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: VU explicitly introduces journalism as a research field and public practice. UCR moving-image foundations are relevant but do not constitute that dedicated journalism introduction.
UCR media archaeology examines technologies and historical communication; no equivalent current media-use research course is asserted.
Dedicated journalism theory-to-practice preparation is distinct from the UCR media and documentary courses.
VU requires newsworthy journalistic articles, verification, sources, editorial teamwork and peer revision. UCR life writing and documentary work do not supply this complete newsroom writing sequence.

Both combine critical audiovisual interpretation with research, interviewing, filming and editing. VU explicitly produces journalistic reels, reportage and explainers; UCR produces a short documentary and studies nonfiction form and ethics.

Both analyze narrative techniques across media. UCR examines medium specificity and literary-film adaptation through a substantial project; VU studies news narratives, truth claims, ethnographic content analysis and membership categorization, which remain distinct.
Both examine how language and textual choices construct meaning. UCR emphasizes stylistics, grammar, cognition and discourse; the complete VU introductory media/communication remit differs.
UCR stylistic and qualitative inquiry contribute relevant analysis. The dedicated standardized written/spoken discourse-analysis and formulation sequence is not duplicated.
Both connect communication and public life. UCR studies public spheres, civil society and empirical public initiatives; VU gives journalism and democracy a dedicated focus.
Both examine persuasion, audience, framing and ethical message choices. UCR applies these through actual community communication and reflective research; contexts and assessments differ.
No full communication-and-cognition counterpart is asserted. UCR stylistics and psychology make narrower contributions elsewhere.

VU teaches inductive conversation analysis, turns and social actions using natural/institutional talk. UCR qualitative/discourse and interviewing work does not establish this specialist sequence; formal entry also remains unresolved.
UCR Ethics makes a real philosophical contribution, but a complete counterpart to the external philosophy course is not established by the retained evidence.
VU applies institutional conversation analysis to journalistic, legal and healthcare interaction. UCR interviews/discourse inquiry are relevant but do not reproduce that dedicated analytical method.
UCR empirical methods and persuasion are relevant; no complete dedicated communication-effects research sequence is asserted.
Ethics, AI responsibility and documentary representation provide contributions, but no dedicated journalism/media-ethics course is asserted.

VU studies cognitive processing of visual/verbal messages, advertising metaphors and instructional images. UCR close visual and persuasive analysis is relevant without duplicating this cognitive-method sequence.
Both develop empirical social-research design and quantitative inquiry. UCR includes surveys/experiments, R analysis and an actual group research project; institutional methods sequences differ.
Both develop academic inquiry, writing, presentation and reflection. UCR adds civic and personal development; it does not implement the VU language-test and remediation gate.
UCR uses writing across research courses, but no scheduled course is asserted as the dedicated VU academic-writing course.

Both find, transform, analyze and visualize numerical/textual data. UCR uses R and multiple data types, including web data; VU additionally requires a newsworthy journalistic story and high-quality visualizations. That editorial formation is not supplied by data methods alone.

Both support empirical statistical inference. UCR applies multivariate regression, ANOVA, logistic and factor methods in R with research reporting; communication-specific applications and the preceding methods sequence differ.
Genuine approved 30-EC open study remains uninstantiated; level/approval restrictions and any consequence of the missing prerequisite are not replaced by invented choices.

VU conducts practice-relevant empirical research for media/journalism organizations. UCR has actual empirical/community projects, but no guaranteed commissioned media-organization research course is supplied.
Required thesis symposium organization, presentation and public-science output are distinct; UCR presentations do not certify this culmination or its access conditions.
